one_line_contribution: That the raw-vs-compressed ordering of reusable agent experience is not a main effect of abstraction but flips sign with writer identity — a reader's own raw trajectories beat its own compressed summaries/procedures at matched tokens, a stranger's raw trajectories lose to the stranger's compressed ones, and at the procedure level the writer becomes undetectable and the whole compressed branch collapses to a static expert prompt.
closest_prior_work: Two verified papers squeeze the contribution from both sides. (a) arXiv:2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (verified via s2cli.py paper, s2 channel, 2026-05-29, 2 citations): controlled experiments across multiple backbones showing that retrieved procedural skills are NOT model-agnostic and that model-conditioned rewriting is needed to make them transfer. This is the single most damaging omission — it is in the brief but appears nowhere in the proposal's Related Work, and P4 ('re-compressing the foreign pool with the reader itself changes nothing; what matters is what compression removes, not who words it') is close to the negation of that paper's headline result. A proposal cannot pre-register the null of a published positive without naming and re-running that method. (b) arXiv:2604.14004, 'Memory Transfer Learning' (verified, s2, 2026-04-15): 'abstraction dictates transferability; high-level insights generalize well, whereas low-level traces often induce negative transfer due to excessive specificity.' That is the proposed interaction shape already reported, with the transfer axis being domain rather than writer. Swapping 'domain' for 'writer' is a real manipulation but a modest conceptual step, and the proposal's own Related Work concedes 2604.14004 and 2605.24117 'occupy one cell each'. Also close: arXiv:2605.23899 (verified, hf) studies the full extraction-to-consumption lifecycle of model-generated skills and reports that effectiveness varies across extractor/consumer scenarios — i.e. writer x reader for skills is already being systematically studied; what remains uniquely the proposal's is the token-matched raw arm inside that matrix.
strongest_objection: P2 — the foreign-cell half of the interaction, without which the title claim dies — is already in trouble from the measurements on the proposal's own node. Measurement C reports, for the Qwen3-32B reader consuming the expert (i.e. foreign) pool at ~430 matched tokens: k=3 raw retrieval = +27 net over k=0, static3 (3 type-conditioned expert exemplars) = +12.4, and the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt instr_all = +9.5 over k=0 and -20.1 under k=3. instr_all is essentially the E-pool L2 cell; k=3 is essentially the E-pool L0 cell. So in the one foreign writer/reader pair already measured, foreign RAW beats foreign PROCEDURES by roughly +17 to +20 net — the exact outcome the proposal declares falsifying for a foreign cell ('raw foreign winning in any single cell falsifies that cell'). The plan responds by demoting E L0 and E L2 to a 2-seed 'descriptive' secondary arm and resting the confirmatory foreign cells on X->Qwen3 and Q->EXAONE, where the same +20-point raw advantage is the obvious prior. The escape hatch — that expert walkthroughs are special because they carry no search and no thoughts — is not free either: P6's point prediction is that thought-stripped foreign raw BEATS foreign raw, which makes the expert pool the best-case foreign raw arm and therefore makes the existing +20 result more damaging, not less. A reviewer will read the proposal as pre-registering, at 6 seeds and ~50 GPU-hours per reader, a prediction its own pilot has already contradicted for the writer it has in hand. Two further structural problems compound this: (i) the headline interaction P3 is pure arithmetic on P1 and P2 (at their stated margins I >= +12 is forced), so the 'headline' contributes no independent test; (ii) P6, the only mechanism test, has a +6 margin against a +-4.2 four-cell half-width, violating the proposal's own 'margin at least twice the half-width' rule, so the predicted and null intervals overlap — the automated entailment check flags it unresolvable and the proposal does not fix it.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Promote the expert-pool cells (E L0 vs E L2 at matched tokens) to 6 seeds and make them a confirmatory foreign cell, or state explicitly and in advance why the already-measured +20 raw advantage for the expert writer does not count as a foreign cell — with a manipulation (thoughts, on-policy search text) that the design isolates rather than an assertion. As written the plan is a well-powered test of a hypothesis the pilot already disfavours. (2) Add a content-matched pool arm: restrict both the self and foreign pools to the intersection of training games that BOTH writers solved, so that 'writer identity' is manipulated with pool membership, task difficulty and type composition held fixed at the game level. The current type-balanced ablation (L0 only, 2 seeds) does not do this. (3) Add a same-backbone-different-scaffold-or-temperature Qwen3-32B writer at 6 seeds as the proximity-at-fixed-capability foreign writer, which the brief makes binding and which the proposal answers only with an optional 2-seed Qwen3-8B arm. Without it, 'writer != reader' is confounded with 'different model family', and the trivial rival — foreign raw traces hurt because of output-format and action-phrasing mismatch, which any normalisation would fix — is untested; template-normalising the foreign raw traces (as is already done for L0s) is the cheap control that separates format from 'writer-specific search'. (4) Re-run a model-conditioned rewriter in the style of 2605.30723 as the P4 arm rather than a plain reader re-compression, and either raise S(r)'s margin to +8.4 or take the four L0/L0s cells to ~12 seeds so P6 can separate its prediction from its null.
missing_baseline: An intersection-matched pool: self and foreign pools restricted to the same set of training games (those both writers solved), at L0 and L2, 6 seeds. Without it the self-vs-foreign contrast confounds writer identity with which games are in each pool and how hard they were — the Qwen3 self pool is documented as type-skewed (pick-and-place 0.81 vs heat 0.26) and the EXAONE pool will be skewed differently, so 'foreign' and 'self' retrieve different content, not merely differently phrased content. Second omission a reviewer will demand: a same-backbone, different-scaffold/temperature Qwen3-32B writer as a proximity-at-fixed-capability foreign writer (the brief makes this binding; the plan offers only an optional 2-seed Qwen3-8B arm), plus a format-normalised foreign-raw control that tests the mundane rival explanation of output-format mismatch.
preprint_collision: No verified collision found, but the check has one hole that matters and one omission that matters more. Queries I ran (channel that answered in brackets): (1) 'abstraction level of transferred agent experience raw trajectories versus summaries versus procedures cross-model' --recent [s2+hf, hf answered]: returned 2608.31100 (S3Gym, experience representation and self-improvement, no writer manipulation), 2606.23127, 2605.24117, 2605.23899, 2604.14004, 2608.20319, 2603.14465 — none crosses abstraction level with writer identity at matched tokens. (2) 'writer identity self-generated versus foreign experience memory reuse same model own trajectories in-context' [s2+hf, hf]: returned 2606.24428 (Execute-Distill-Verify, heterogeneous agents build experience to escape a self-confirmation trap — adjacent and arguably in tension with the self-pool advantage the proposal predicts), 2605.12978, 2606.04703, 2605.20616; no collision. (3) 'compression of agent memory raises transferability survey memory skills rules abstraction hierarchy' [s2+hf, hf]: returned 2602.03315 (Memora, abstraction-vs-specificity trade-off in memory representation), 2601.07470 (MCMA, learnable memory abstraction, negative transfer under distribution shift), 2512.13564 (agent-memory survey), 2607.01224 — none is the survey the proposal cites. (4) closest named method, 'SkillEvolBench episodic experience to procedural skills raw trajectory reuse outperforms distilled skills token-matched' [s2+hf, both]: confirmed 2605.24117 and surfaced 2606.26669 (SKILL-DISCO), 2606.01139 (SkillRevise, cross-model transferability of revised skills), 2608.03874, 2606.13317 — none manipulates writer identity against raw traces at matched tokens. (5) home-literature 'self-generated demonstrations beat other-model demonstrations in-context learning familiarity of exemplars own outputs' --recent [s2+hf, hf]: only 3 hits, nearest 2605.26350 ('When Correct Demonstrations Hurt') — the home vocabulary is essentially empty here, which is a mild positive for the in-context self-vs-foreign framing. ID verification (s2cli.py paper): VERIFIED 2605.24117, 2604.14004, 2605.12978, 2606.23127, 2608.07169, 2605.30723, 2605.23899; also seen in search output with matching abstracts 2601.07470, 2606.01139. COULD NOT VERIFY 2604.15877 — 'not found on S2 or HF' on two separate attempts. That is the survey asserting 'transferability rises with compression', i.e. one of the two poles of the Short Hypothesis, the Abstract's opening sentence and the framing of the entire contribution; the proposal's collision check lists it in prose but never says it verified it. A submission whose headline is 'these two published positions are two cells of one interaction' must be able to produce both positions. The graver omission is that the check never searched for, and the Related Work never mentions, 2605.30723 (Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All, verified) even though the brief hands it to the author — a paper reporting exactly the model-dependence of skill utility that P4 pre-registers as null. Otherwise the check is above average for this round: it states its queries, its channels and its IDs, and it verified 2606.23127 itself.
